intro.title: Why I'm Here
intro.quote: Poetry teaches us to choose every word with devotion and care, and invites us to listen to them with tenderness and awe. In this simple act, we find the purest foundation of love.
intro.body:
This is my space to express myself as I've fallen in love with poetry.

It's a form of therapy. It gives me breath while taking my breath away. It's where my love lives. It's where I can be understood. It's where I grow. 

I take my inspiration from so many places: creators I admire with aching devotion, like Quinlan Walther; poets who crack me wide open, especially Emily Dickinson (and the series that feel so fucking raw and alive I can hardly breathe through it); and amateur poets like Luke Bateman and other anonymous poets on Tumblr. 

I read and write my way back to myself, one poem at a time. 

My Infinite Adore, when your heart is ready, you'll know where to find me.

analyses.title: Forever — is composed of Nows —
analyses.author: Emily Dickinson
analyses.excerpt:
Forever — is composed of Nows —
'Tis not a different time —
Except for Infiniteness —
And Latitude of Home —
analyses.fullText:
Forever — is composed of Nows —
'Tis not a different time —
Except for Infiniteness —
And Latitude of Home —

From this — experienced Here —
Remove the Dates — to These —
Let Months dissolve in Further Months —
And Years — exhale in Years —

Without Debate — or Pause —
Or Celebrated Days —
No different Our Years would be
From Anno Dominies —
analyses.analysis:
I return to this poem the way some people return to a prayer... with the kind of reverence that makes my breath stutter and my chest warm all at once. God, just writing this makes me emotional. Every time I read it, I feel a physical shift in me. It's as if something in my ribs catches fire all while another part of me drops into a sudden frozen stillness. It's not an abstract poem to me... it's a fully lived spiritual experience. It's magic, right here.
 
Dickinson does something in this poem that I can barely articulate... she collapses eternity into the present moment so completely that I literally feel the world sharpen around me. My heart pulls tight. There’s heat. There’s cold. And there’s a strange sensation of revelation, like something just clicks and falls into place in my heart.
 
When she writes that *forever* isn't somewhere else, not later, not after death, but here—*right here*—I literally feel the truth of it in my chest. Eternity is in the now. In every breath. Right here, in presence.
 
Years ago, I engraved this line “Forever is composed of Nows” on the back of my favourite watch. It was a vow to myself before I even fully understood it. A vow to be intentional with my energy, my love, my time. A vow to notice, to listen, and to be amazed by the small things that create the now.
 
And now, rereading this poem years later, I see what I failed to understand back then... that all of this insistence on the present circles back to **love**! Love as attention. Love as devotion. Love as presence strong enough to stretch a single moment into infinity. With just a few words, she's able to collapse infinity into a single moment while also stretching the present into inifity... only a genius can accomplish something of this magnitude.
 
She also dismantles time in such a sensual way... stripping away the dates, the calendars, the "celebrated days" and what’s left is not emptiness but the raw and bare moment itself. Reading it, I feel something holy. It's literally that for me, a spiritual/religious experience. This idea that if we lived with that kind of awareness, our years would be indistinguishable from God’s own. Isn't this magical?!
 
*Forever is not a place we go, but a way of being here.* And every time a moment of love makes me forget the shape of time, I understand her a little more.
 
This poem doesn’t just speak to me... no, it rearranges me.

originals.title: My Infinite Adore
originals.text:
My Infinite Adore
I lay each stone in silence
a dwelling untouched
For when your heart remembers
our unwritten pages
The walls will wake
to whisper the version of us
time was too young to hold

originals.title: Rubberband
originals.text:
I got this rubberband on my wrist
and i snap it every time that i think about your lips
I got this rubberband on my wrist
almost break it every time that i'm trying to forget
I got this rubberband on my wrist
and i snap it every time to remember you exist
I got this rubberband on my wrist
and I break it every time I remember the promise I still haven't kept yet

originals.title: Through your eyes
originals.text:
Do you still see the ghost I used to be?
Or do I wear his shadow on my skin?
Am I forever tethered to his memory?
Or can you see where I begin?

I've shed the past like borrowed sin,
do you still mistake the ashes for the flame?
As I rise, untouched by him,
will I be someone you love again?

originals.title: Grilled Cheese
originals.text:
I'm Noah, eyes always wet, waiting for the door to open.
But the house I'm building isn't wood or paint.
It's the four walls, the roof, and the door of my heart.
Untouched by the scars.

And the soft breath I'm left with in your absence,
barely enough to keep me alive,
feeds the light on the front porch.

So when that knob finally turns,
you can sit at the table,
and I'll make you a grilled cheese.
